records.name: Philly Fixers Guild
records.summary: Volunteers who fix broken household items for neighbors at free Repair Fairs around the city. You bring the item, and a volunteer works through the fix with you.
records.what_you_do: Fix items at Repair Fairs, teach the troubleshooting steps, or answer repair questions through Ask a Fixer.

schedule.text: Free Repair Fairs on Thursdays from 6 to 8 pm at NextFab, with fairs posted on the group's calendar.

requirements.gear: Bring the broken item (one you can carry in) and any replacement part you already know you need.

first_step.how: Bring a broken household item to a Thursday evening Repair Fair at NextFab. Email the volunteer contact or join the Repair Fair list to hear about each fair.
first_step.basis: Fairs are open to anyone with an item to fix, and the group says volunteers without repair skills are welcome and that a Fixer guides you through the repair.
first_step.what_to_expect: You stay with your item and do the troubleshooting yourself, with a volunteer Fixer guiding each step. Check-in happens at a triage table before the repair. The fair runs for two hours, from 6 to 8 pm, and costs nothing. Repairs are done by volunteers who are not necessarily licensed, and nothing comes with a warranty.
first_visit_tips: Bring the whole item and any spare part you already know you need.
Plan to stay for the repair, since dropping an item off is not allowed.
Join the Repair Fair email list to hear about each fair's date.
If you cannot make a fair, use the Ask a Fixer page to get advice on fixing the item at home.

records.notes: Site has no FAQ, parking, transit or accessibility details, so those are left out. Registration for a fair is not stated; the site offers an email list. The volunteer page welcomes people without repair skills and asks for an email to start.

records.name: Philly Kickball League
records.summary: A recreational adult kickball league. Teams play on Sunday afternoons in spring and early summer at Starr Garden on Lombard Street.
records.what_you_do: Register for the season, get placed on a team or as a free agent, and play Sunday games with a playoff session at the end.

schedule.text: Sunday games from 2 to 6 pm in spring and early summer, with a playoff session at the end of the season. The next season is not posted yet.

cost.text: The league does not list a fee on its site, and says all fees go back into the league. Confirm the current price on the registration page before you sign up.

requirements.gear: Plastic cleats only, since metal cleats are not allowed. The league provides the ball, and gear that gives an advantage, such as receiving gloves or steel toes, is not allowed.

first_step.how: Register for the season through the league's registration page. Choose the free agent option if you do not have a team, and sign the liability waiver before you play.
first_step.basis: The 2026 registration page recommends a no-cost exhibition game for new players, regardless of experience, with rules, kicking basics and a short scrimmage, and it offers a free agent option for people without a team.
first_step.what_to_expect: Games run on Sundays from 2 to 6 pm on the Starr Garden field, with up to 10 players on the field and substitutes allowed for up to half a regular season roster. Each team needs a mix of players, and a team that cannot field at least eight players forfeits. Rain and storm calls are made up to an hour before game time, and games can be rescheduled for poor air quality.
first_visit_tips: Arrive on time, because a player who is more than 10 minutes late can leave the team short or cause a forfeit.
Wear plastic cleats only; the league provides the ball.
Sign the liability waiver after you register, before you play.
Check the league site for weather and heat calls before you travel.

records.notes: The site has no FAQ page (the path returned 404), so questions go to the email on the site. The 2026 spring season ran April 12 to July 26 and the 2027 season is not posted. Older press figures for the fee are not repeated here because the league site does not list one. Team placement for new players is not stated beyond the free agent option. Newcomer rating is 4 because of the new player exhibition game, which applies to the 2026 spring season.

records.name: Range of Motion Philly
records.summary: A studio in Center City with martial arts, parkour, dance and music classes for kids, teens and adults, plus school break camps and a summer camp.
records.what_you_do: Join an after-school or school break class for kids, or start adult martial arts after a one on one consultation. Email the studio to set up the consultation.

schedule.text: Adult martial arts and dance classes run through the year. After-school classes run during the school year, with school break camps and a summer camp.

cost.text: Adult memberships are paid monthly, and the site lists several prices, roughly $110 to $195 a month depending on classes and discounts. Youth after-school registration is $100 per child, plus monthly fees. Confirm current prices with the studio before you join.

first_step.how: Email Rangeofmotion@gmail.com to set up a one on one consultation for adult martial arts. For kids, use the early registration form for after-school or class programs.
first_step.basis: Adult martial arts requires a one on one consultation and a paid first month before you can join, and the site lists no drop in option. Youth programs need a registration fee and forms before the first class.
first_step.what_to_expect: Adult martial arts classes last about 1 to 2 hours and mix bag work, pad and mitt drills, and partner exchanges, with strength and conditioning included. The first step is a one on one consultation, where you can ask about your level. A first month of membership is charged after that.
first_visit_tips: Book the one on one consultation before you come, and ask about your level then.
Ask the studio what to wear and where to arrive, since the site does not say.
Plan for a 1 to 2 hour class; mobility and drilling sessions last one hour.
Read the cancellation terms before you pay: cancelling takes effect 30 days after you give notice, and a fee applies inside that window.

records.notes: Prices conflict across the studio's pages. The home page advertises a $25 intro month and a free trial lesson, but the martial arts page says the first month costs $40 after a required consultation and is not free, so this record follows the martial arts page. Membership pages list $129 and $135 a month for standard adult classes, with discounts. The adult dance page and the adult classes page returned 404. No accessibility, drop in or language details are published. The rates page says cancellations were not allowed after April 2024, which looks outdated, so ask the studio.

records.name: Rotary Club of Philadelphia
records.summary: A Rotary club of business and professional members, part of Rotary District 7450. It focuses its service on people in need, mostly in Philadelphia and some abroad.
records.what_you_do: Come to an evening meeting with a speaker, sign up for a service day such as a cemetery cleanup, or join a fundraising walk team.

schedule.text: Evening meetings at 6 pm on the first Thursday of the month at the Pyramid Club. Service days and social events are posted on the club calendar.

cost.text: Dues and guest fees are not published. Some events are ticketed, such as a concert with paid tickets.

first_step.how: Register for the next Thursday meeting through the online form on the club's site, or sign up for a service day on the club calendar.
first_step.basis: Meetings and service days are posted publicly with online sign up, and the club says guests are part of the audience. The club does not publish a guest policy, so the rating stays at 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: A meeting is an evening at 6 pm with a speaker who talks for about 20 to 25 minutes, followed by questions. Usually 30 to 60 members and guests attend, mostly professionals and civic leaders. Service days are hands on volunteer work the club organizes, such as a cemetery cleanup.
first_visit_tips: Register through the meeting form before the date, since that is how the club counts guests.
Ask the club about guest meal costs and dress when you register, because the site does not say.
Ask about any dues before you join, since the club does not publish them.

records.notes: The membership page URL returned 404. Membership goes through an online form that this agent did not submit. Dues, guest policy, meal cost and venue accessibility are not published. The next meeting listed is November 5, 2026 at the Pyramid Club. The Gundaker Foundation affiliate is listed in leads_only.

records.name: Schuylkill Center for Environmental Education
records.summary: A nature center in Roxborough with woods, fields, and trails. Volunteers help with its yearly Winter Bird Census and with seasonal work days.
records.what_you_do: Count birds on the yearly Winter Bird Census, plant trees or native plants on volunteer days, join monthly restoration workdays, or volunteer at the Wildlife Clinic.

schedule.text: Restoration workdays run monthly. Wildlife Clinic support volunteers work two 4 hour shifts a month, and animal care volunteers commit to one 4 hour shift a week. Volunteer training is offered a few times a year.

cost.text: Volunteering and the Winter Bird Census are free.

first_step.how: For event days such as the Winter Bird Census or a planting day, use the Sign Up link on the event page. For the Wildlife Clinic, apply online, attend an information session, sign the volunteer agreement, and finish the online ethics and safety courses before a first shift.
first_step.basis: The Winter Bird Census page says birders of any skill level are welcome, no experience is needed, and it has a sign up link. Clinic shifts need an application and training first, so that route rates lower.
first_step.what_to_expect: Event days last a few hours and are free, with hands on tasks such as planting, decorating the greenhouse, or counting birds by sight and sound. Wildlife Clinic volunteers go through an application, an information session, a waiver and online training before their first shift. Food and drinks are provided on the Winter Bird Census morning.
first_visit_tips: Sign up through the event link ahead of time, since the events list does not show how to register.
Bring a donation if you like; the clinic suggests paper towels, cotton balls, trash bags, or dish soap.
Check the age rules first: clinic support starts at 16 and animal care at 18, and group workdays need one adult for every 10 to 12 children.
Ask the Center about parking and transit when you call, since the site does not list them.

records.notes: The Winter Bird Census page we read is dated February 8, 2025 and has passed, so the census is treated as a yearly February event. The tier 1 source ?p=279962 now shows Wildlife Clinic volunteer training, not the census. The volunteer office phone (215) 853-6248 is listed on the volunteer page; the main line is kept. Regular volunteers who work with children need free Pennsylvania clearances, but the page does not say that clinic or event roles need them, so none is recorded. Court-mandated service hours are not accepted, per the volunteer page. Service hour letters are requested by email; the page does not promise them, so that field is unknown. No accessibility, parking or transit information is published.

records.name: Speakeasy Open Mic at the Kelly Writers House
records.summary: A monthly open mic at the Kelly Writers House on Penn's campus. Anyone can sign up at the podium for a short slot and read poems, prose, or other short performances.
records.what_you_do: Sign up when you arrive for a three minute slot and perform, or come to listen and take part in the room.

schedule.text: Open mic evenings at 7 pm, held in person at the Writers House. The listing shows one upcoming session and does not give a fixed monthly pattern.

cost.text: The listing does not say whether there is a cost.

first_step.how: Register on the online form if you plan to attend in person. To perform, sign up at the podium when you arrive; each slot is three minutes.
first_step.basis: Anyone can sign up at the podium for a three minute slot, but the listing asks attendees to register online first and does not say that beginners are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Performers sign up when they arrive and get a three minute slot to read poems, prose, or other short pieces. The room is student run and also open to people who only want to listen. The listing does not say what it costs or how many readers take part.
first_visit_tips: Register on the online form ahead of time if you plan to attend.
Arrive early enough to sign the podium sheet if you want to read.
Bring a short piece, since each slot is three minutes.

records.notes: The NSO page describes a one time August 20, 2026 event for the incoming class, so it is not used for the schedule. The listing does not say whether the open mic is limited to Penn people, so open_to stays public from tier 1. The monthly pattern from tier 1 is not confirmed on the current listing. The listing gives no accessibility details and no contact person.

records.name: Special Olympics Pennsylvania, Greater Philadelphia Region
records.summary: The Pennsylvania Special Olympics program covers Philadelphia and four nearby counties. It runs year-round sports for athletes with intellectual disabilities, plus free health screenings through its Healthy Athletes program.
records.what_you_do: Train and compete as an athlete, or volunteer in one of many roles, from coaching to event help. Unified partners play on teams alongside athletes.

schedule.text: Sports and training run on schedules that vary by sport and location. Use the sport finder to find one near you. Volunteers can ask questions on a monthly online info call on the fourth Wednesday, 6:30 to 7:30 pm.

locations.label: Greater Philadelphia Region office, Norristown
locations.address: 2570 Boulevard of the Generals, Suite 124, Norristown, PA 19403

cost.text: Athletic training and competitions are at no cost to athletes, per the state site.

first_step.how: Athletes: create an athlete profile on the state portal and finish the health screening. Volunteers: start through the volunteer opportunities page and come to the monthly info call first.
first_step.basis: Athletes and volunteers both have a clear way in, including a no-pressure monthly info call, but the site describes no beginner day, and athletes need a formal identification of eligibility first.
first_step.what_to_expect: Staff hold a monthly online info call on the fourth Wednesday, 6:30 to 7:30 pm, to answer questions about volunteer roles. Event volunteers help at one-day or multi-day competitions with scorekeeping, awards, and setup or cleanup, for about 2 to 8 hours on event day only. Athletes register on the state portal, complete a short health screening, and train at no cost.
first_visit_tips: Join the monthly info call first; it is a question session, not a sign up.
Athletes need a formal identification of eligibility from an agency or professional before they register.
Every volunteer needs volunteer registration; local program and some coaching roles also need training and a background check.
Call 610-630-9450 or use the contact page; the state team says it replies within two business days.

records.notes: Athletes must be 8 or older; ages 2 to 7 take part through Young Athletes, so min_age stays 2. Background checks are required for local program volunteers and for unified partners, assistant coaches, team volunteers and head coaches who are 18 or older; event volunteers have none listed. The region covers Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery and Philadelphia counties. The regional email appears only behind a protected link, so it is not recorded; use the contact page at specialolympicspa.org/contact-us/. No accessibility information is published.
